Beyond Vision: Crafting Effective Alt Text for a More Inclusive Web

2026-05-12 3 min read

Alt text is more than just a description; it's a vital gateway to information for users relying on screen readers. Learn how well-crafted alt text enhances accessibility and enriches the user experience for everyone.

In the visual landscape of the internet, images play a crucial role in conveying information, emotion, and branding. However, for the millions of people who are blind or have low vision, these images are invisible without proper context. This is where 'alt text' (alternative text) comes into play. Alt text provides a textual description of an image, allowing screen readers to verbally convey its content to users, ensuring they don't miss out on vital information or context.

Crafting effective alt text isn't just about describing what you see; it's about conveying the image's purpose and content concisely. When writing alt text, focus on conveying the essential information or function of the image. Ask yourself: 'If the image weren't there, what text would I use to convey the same information?' Avoid redundant phrases like 'image of...' or 'picture of...' and prioritize clarity and conciseness. For example, instead of 'Picture of a dog in a park,' consider 'Golden retriever playing fetch in a sunny park.'

Remember that not every image requires extensive alt text; purely decorative images should have an empty alt="" attribute to prevent screen readers from announcing them unnecessarily. Implementing thoughtful alt text is a simple yet powerful step towards a more accessible web, ensuring your content is understandable and usable by all.
